title: Mixed reading
goal: Read short everyday documents (notices, menus, texts, ads, signs and posters) and find the information you need.

example.fr: Le café est ouvert de 7 h à 15 h.
example.en: The café is open from 7 a.m. to 3 p.m.

example.fr: La bibliothèque est fermée le lundi.
example.en: The library is closed on Mondays.

items.note: Only for price. Free time is libre.
On a menu, une entrée is a starter, not a main course.

steps.title: Three everyday documents
steps.intro: You don't need to understand every word. Read the question first, then look for the answer.

blocks.title: A notice in the lobby
blocks.context: On the wall next to the mailboxes in an apartment building in Montréal.
blocks.fr:
AVIS AUX LOCATAIRES
Mardi 14 octobre, de 9 h à 12 h : pas d'eau chaude dans l'immeuble.
Un technicien va travailler au sous-sol.
Des questions ? Appelez le concierge au 514 555-0172.
Merci de votre patience !
La gestion de l'immeuble
blocks.en: NOTICE TO TENANTS. Tuesday, October 14, from 9 a.m. to 12 p.m.: no hot water in the building. A technician is going to work in the basement. Questions? Call the superintendent at 514-555-0172. Thank you for your patience! Building management

blocks.prompt: When is there no hot water?
blocks.explain: [[Mardi]] is Tuesday, and [[de 9 h à 12 h]] means from 9 to 12: the morning only.

blocks.title: The menu board at a café
blocks.context: A small café near a metro station.
blocks.fr:
CAFÉ DU COIN — MENU DU JOUR
Soupe du jour : 5,50 $
Sandwich jambon-fromage : 8,75 $
Salade César : 9,25 $
Muffin aux bleuets : 3,25 $
Café ou thé : 2,50 $
SPÉCIAL DU MIDI : soupe + sandwich + café = 14 $
Ouvert du lundi au samedi, de 7 h à 15 h
blocks.en: THE CORNER CAFÉ — TODAY'S MENU. Soup of the day: $5.50. Ham and cheese sandwich: $8.75. Caesar salad: $9.25. Blueberry muffin: $3.25. Coffee or tea: $2.50. LUNCH SPECIAL: soup + sandwich + coffee = $14. Open Monday to Saturday, 7 a.m. to 3 p.m.

blocks.prompt: At lunchtime, you want soup, a sandwich and a coffee. How much do you pay?
blocks.explain: Separately it is $16.75, but the [[spécial du midi]] (lunch special; a Québec anglicism, see the Canada note) gives you all three for $14.
optionFeedback: That's the price of the three things separately. Look at the special.

blocks.title: A text message
blocks.context: Karim is waiting for his friend at the café.
blocks.fr: Salut Karim ! Je suis en retard, désolée ! Mon bus n'arrive pas… J'arrive au café vers 18 h 30. Tu peux commander pour moi ? Un thé et un muffin, s'il te plaît. Merci ! Sofia
blocks.en: Hi Karim! I'm late, sorry! My bus isn't coming… I'll get to the café around 6:30 p.m. Can you order for me? A tea and a muffin, please. Thanks! Sofia

blocks.prompt: What does Sofia ask Karim to do?
blocks.explain: [[Tu peux commander pour moi ?]] — commander means to order. The tea and the muffin tell you it's about food.

blocks.title: Five reading strategies
blocks.body:
You already know enough French to read most signs and short messages. The trick is to **stop translating word by word**.

- **Look at the shape first.** A title in capitals, prices, a phone number: you know if it is a menu, an ad or a notice before you read a single word.
- **Read the question first.** Then you know what to look for.
- **Scan for numbers.** A question about *when* or *how much*? Look only for numbers with **h**, **$** or a day of the week.
- **Use cognates.** Many words look like English: [[technicien]], [[musique]], [[parc]], [[idéal]], [[salade]], [[patience]].
- **Guess from context.** In [[pas d'eau chaude dans l'immeuble]], you know *eau chaude*. The notice is for tenants, so [[immeuble]] is probably *building*. You're right!

blocks.title: How numbers look on signs
head: You read
You say
It means
blocks.note: Signs use the **24-hour clock**: subtract 12 from anything after 12 h. Prices use a **comma** where English uses a point, and the **$ comes after** the number.

blocks.title: Words you see on signs and documents
Try it: a small ad
blocks.context: On a community notice board in Ottawa.
blocks.fr:
À VENDRE
Vélo pour femme, bleu, en très bon état.
Prix : 120 $
Idéal pour aller au travail ou à l'université !
Appelez Olivier au 613 555-0148, le soir après 18 h.
Ottawa, quartier Vanier
blocks.en: FOR SALE. Woman's bike, blue, in very good condition. Price: $120. Ideal for going to work or to university! Call Olivier at 613-555-0148, in the evening after 6 p.m. Ottawa, Vanier neighbourhood.

blocks.explain: [[le soir]] = in the evening, and [[après 18 h]] = after 6 p.m. Scan for the number with **h**.

blocks.title: Try it: opening hours
blocks.context: On the door of a public library.
blocks.fr:
BIBLIOTHÈQUE MUNICIPALE DE GATINEAU
Heures d'ouverture
Lundi : fermé
Du mardi au vendredi : de 10 h à 20 h
Samedi et dimanche : de 10 h à 17 h
Fermé le 25 décembre et le 1er janvier
blocks.en: GATINEAU PUBLIC LIBRARY. Opening hours. Monday: closed. Tuesday to Friday: 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. Saturday and Sunday: 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. Closed on December 25 and January 1.

blocks.prompt: It's Wednesday, 7 p.m. Is the library open?
blocks.explain: Wednesday ([[mercredi]]) is between Tuesday and Friday, so it's open [[de 10 h à 20 h]]. 20 h = 8 p.m.

blocks.title: Try it: an event poster
blocks.context: In the window of a community centre in Montréal.
blocks.fr:
FÊTE DE QUARTIER
Samedi 20 septembre, de 11 h à 16 h
Parc La Fontaine, Montréal
Musique, jeux pour les enfants, cuisine du monde
Entrée gratuite !
Apportez un pique-nique et des chaises.
Info : Centre communautaire, 514 555-0190
blocks.en: NEIGHBOURHOOD PARTY. Saturday, September 20, 11 a.m. to 4 p.m. La Fontaine Park, Montréal. Music, games for children, food from around the world. Free admission! Bring a picnic and chairs. Info: Community centre, 514-555-0190.

blocks.prompt: How much does it cost to go to the party?
blocks.explain: [[Entrée gratuite]] = free admission. The other numbers are times and the date: a classic trap.

blocks.title: False friends on signs
blocks.body:
Some words look like English but mean something else:

- [[librairie]] = **bookstore**. A library is a [[bibliothèque]].
- [[location]] = **rental** ([[location de vélos]] = bike rental).
- [[entrée]] on a menu = **starter**, not the main course. On a poster, it means admission.
- On doors: [[Poussez]] = **push**, [[Tirez]] = **pull**. [[Sortie]] = exit.
- [[Fermé]] and [[ouvert]] are the two most useful words on any door!

Documents in Québec have a few local features:

- [[bleuets]] are blueberries (in France: [[myrtilles]]).
- Lunch is [[le dîner]] in Québec. Restaurant boards often say [[spécial du midi]] (lunch special): this is a common Québec **anglicism** (from English *special*). The standard terms are [[menu du midi]] or, for a full set meal with several courses, [[table d'hôte]]. Recognize *spécial*, but write *menu du midi*.
- Prices are written [[5,50 $]]: comma for cents, dollar sign after.
- Area codes help you place a document: 514 and 438 (Montréal), 418 (Québec City), 819 (Gatineau), 613 (Ottawa), 506 (New Brunswick).
- In apartment buildings, the person who looks after the building is often called [[le concierge]].

blocks.title: Listen and repeat
blocks.note: Reading signs aloud helps you remember them. Say the numbers in full.

lines.tip: du lundi au samedi = from Monday to Saturday.

lines.fr: De dix heures à vingt heures.
lines.tip: The sign says 10 h – 20 h; you say heures.
5,50 $ — the number, then dollars, then the cents.
You hear the t in gratuite because of the final -e.
A man writes désolé; it sounds the same.

blocks.fr: La bibliothèque est fermée le lundi.
blocks.en: The library is closed on Mondays.

blocks.fr: Le spécial du midi coûte quatorze dollars.
blocks.en: The lunch special costs fourteen dollars.
blocks.prompt: How much is the lunch special?
blocks.explain: [[quatorze]] (14) has two syllables with a z sound; [[quatre]] (4) is short; [[quarante]] (40) ends in a nasal *an*.

steps.title: New signs, your turn
steps.intro: These are new mini-documents. Use the strategies: question first, then scan.

blocks.prompt: A shop door says: “Fermé le dimanche”. What does it mean?
blocks.explain: [[fermé]] = closed, and [[le]] + day = every week on that day.

blocks.prompt: A text says: “Je suis en retard. J'arrive vers 19 h.” What is the message?
options: The person is late and will arrive around 7 p.m.
The person is early and is already there.
The person can't come at 7 p.m.

blocks.text: La bibliothèque est ___ le samedi, de 10 h à 17 h.
blocks.en: The library is open on Saturdays, from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m.
blocks.explain: There are opening times, so it's open; [[bibliothèque]] is feminine, so add -e: [[ouverte]].

blocks.prompt: Match the sign words with their meaning.
A restaurant board says: “Menu du midi : 16 $”. When can you get this price?
The café is closed on Sundays.
accept: Le café est fermé le dimanche.
Le café est fermé les dimanches.
blocks.hint: le + day = every week on that day.
blocks.explain: [[café]] is masculine, so [[fermé]] has no extra -e. [[le dimanche]] = on Sundays.

blocks.prompt: An ad says: “Table à vendre, 40 $. Appelez Mei le matin.” When should you call?
blocks.explain: [[le matin]] = in the morning. The 40 is the price, not a time.
[[du]] = de + le, [[au]] = à + le: from Monday to Friday.

blocks.text: Il n'y a pas ___ eau chaude mardi matin.
blocks.en: There is no hot water on Tuesday morning.
blocks.explain: After a negative ([[pas]]), [[de l']] becomes [[d']]: pas d'eau.

blocks.prompt: A poster says: “Cours de yoga gratuit — samedi 10 h — Centre communautaire”. Which is true?
options: The class is free, on Saturday at 10 a.m.
The class is on Sunday at 10 p.m.

blocks.prompt: You are selling something (a table, a bike, a sofa…). Write a small ad for a notice board: what it is, its colour or condition, the price, and how and when to contact you.
blocks.promptFr: Écrivez une petite annonce : vous vendez un objet.
checklist: The object with an adjective (colour, size or condition)
How to contact you (Appelez… / phone number)
When to call (le matin, le soir, après 18 h…)

models.en: FOR SALE: small grey sofa, $80. Call Raj on Saturdays, 9 a.m. to 12 p.m.: 613-555-0129.

summary:
- Read notices, menus, text messages, ads, opening hours and posters
- Find times, prices and days quickly: [[de 10 h à 20 h]], [[5,50 $]], [[du lundi au samedi]]
- Use cognates and context to guess new words, and watch for false friends like [[librairie]]
